name: Plitvice Lakes
tagline: Sixteen terraced lakes cascading into each other through travertine dams, connected by wooden boardwalks that put you right at the water's edge.
highlight: Standing on a boardwalk with turquoise water flowing directly beneath your feet, Veliki Slap thundering into the pool ahead.
shortDescription: Croatia's most famous national park, sixteen terraced turquoise lakes cascading into each other through travertine dams and waterfalls.
metaDescription: A Plitvice Lakes travel guide: Veliki Slap, the Upper and Lower Lakes, Lake Kozjak, boardwalk hiking, food and how to plan a visit.
nearestAirport: Zagreb Airport (ZAG), about 2 hours by road
knownFor: Veliki Slap waterfall, turquoise cascading lakes, wooden boardwalks
budget: €100–200 per day, mid-range (park entry plus nearby lodging)

intro: Plitvice Lakes is Croatia's most famous natural attraction, sixteen terraced lakes cascading into each other through travertine barriers built up naturally over thousands of years.
Wooden boardwalks wind directly over and beside the water, putting visitors within touching distance of pools so clear the fish seem to hover in mid-air.
It's a full-day destination at minimum, the park's scale meaning even a focused visit to the Lower and Upper Lakes takes several hours of walking.

whyVisit.intro: Plitvice Lakes' case rests on natural scenery that looks retouched even in an unedited photograph.

points.title: The water's colour is not exaggerated in photos
points.text: Mineral content and algae give the lakes their striking, near-unbelievable turquoise.

points.title: The boardwalks put you right at the water's edge
points.text: Wooden paths cross directly over cascades and along the shoreline throughout the park.

points.title: It's one of Europe's oldest national parks
points.text: Protected since 1949 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.

points.title: The scale is bigger than photos suggest
points.text: Sixteen interconnected lakes span a network of trails covering real distance.

points.title: It works well as a Zagreb-to-coast stopover
points.text: Conveniently positioned between the capital and the Dalmatian coast.

attractionsIntro: The park's essential sights are its cascading lakes, waterfalls and the boardwalks connecting them.

attractions.name: Veliki Slap (the Great Waterfall)

image.file: File:The Big Waterfall (Veliki Slap) in Plitvice Lakes National Park, Croatia (48607655996).jpg
image.alt: Veliki Slap, the Great Waterfall at Plitvice Lakes

attractions.text: The park's tallest and most famous waterfall, dropping 78 metres at the end of the Lower Lakes.
attractions.tip: The viewing platform gets crowded — arrive early or late in the day for a clearer view.

attractions.name: The Lower Lakes' cascades

image.alt: Cascading waterfalls in the Lower Lakes at Plitvice

attractions.text: A dramatic run of smaller waterfalls and travertine terraces leading down toward Veliki Slap.
attractions.tip: The most photogenic stretch of boardwalk in the entire park.

attractions.name: The Upper Lakes' turquoise terraces

image.alt: Turquoise terraced lakes in the Upper Lakes area of Plitvice

attractions.text: Quieter and wilder-feeling than the Lower Lakes, forested terraces stepping gently down the valley.
attractions.tip: Allow a full morning or afternoon if you want to properly cover this section.

attractions.name: Lake Kozjak

image.alt: Lake Kozjak, the largest lake at Plitvice

attractions.text: The park's largest lake, crossed by an electric tourist boat connecting the Lower and Upper sections.
attractions.tip: Factor the boat crossing into your route planning — it's included in the park entry ticket.

attractions.name: The wooden boardwalks

image.alt: Wooden boardwalks over the water at Plitvice Lakes

attractions.text: The park's defining feature, paths winding directly over cascades and along shorelines throughout.
attractions.tip: Wear non-slip shoes — the boardwalks can be damp and slippery, especially near waterfalls.

attractions.name: Šupljara Cave
attractions.text: A short, easy detour, a shallow cave the boardwalk trail passes directly through.
attractions.tip: A nice change of pace and shade partway through a longer walking route.

attractions.name: The electric boat across Kozjak

image.alt: An electric tourist boat crossing Lake Kozjak at Plitvice

attractions.text: A restful, scenic interlude between long stretches of walking, included in the park entry fee.
attractions.tip: Check the timetable at the boat dock — services run on a schedule rather than continuously.

thingsToDoIntro: Plitvice rewards a full day of walking, best planned around one of the park's marked routes.

thingsToDo.title: Walk beneath Veliki Slap
thingsToDo.text: An essential stop, the boardwalk bringing you close enough to feel the waterfall's spray.
thingsToDo.tip: One of the busiest single spots in the park — patience pays off for an uncrowded photo.

thingsToDo.title: Cross the boardwalks over turquoise water

image.file: File:Croatia-00890 - Looking Down from the Path (9453374462).jpg
image.alt: Boardwalks crossing turquoise water at Plitvice

thingsToDo.text: A magical, sustained experience, following wooden paths directly over and beside the cascading lakes.
thingsToDo.tip: Pace yourself — the full boardwalk network covers real distance across a full day.

thingsToDo.title: Take the electric boat across Lake Kozjak

image.file: File:Tourist boat on Kozjak lake in Plitvice Lakes National Park, Croatia (48670473892).jpg
image.alt: The electric boat crossing Lake Kozjak

thingsToDo.text: A relaxing way to cover ground, gliding across the park's largest lake between the Lower and Upper sections.
thingsToDo.tip: A nice rest for tired legs partway through a longer route.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Šupljara Cave
thingsToDo.text: A quick, fun detour, the boardwalk trail leading straight through this shallow cave.
thingsToDo.tip: Easy to combine with the main Lower Lakes walking route.

thingsToDo.title: Hike the Upper Lakes trail

image.alt: Hiking the Upper Lakes trail at Plitvice

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding, quieter alternative to the busier Lower Lakes, with a more forested, wild feel.
thingsToDo.tip: Start here first if you'd like to see the park before the day's crowds build.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph the cascading pools

image.alt: Cascading turquoise pools at Plitvice Lakes

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding pursuit throughout the park, with new photogenic terraces around nearly every bend.
thingsToDo.tip: Visit after rain for the waterfalls at their fullest, most dramatic flow.

foodIntro: Food near the park means hearty Lika region cooking, built around lamb, trout and local honey.

foods.name: Lička janjetina (Lika lamb)
foods.text: A real regional specialty, lamb from the Lika region's mountain pastures, often slow-roasted.

foods.name: Ćevapi

image.alt: Ćevapi, grilled minced meat skewers popular across Croatia

foods.text: A reliable, filling classic found throughout continental Croatia, grilled minced meat served with flatbread.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants near the park's entrances and along the main road.

foods.name: Fresh river trout
foods.text: A natural fit for the region's clean, cold waterways, simply grilled or pan-fried.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants near the park, especially those along the Korana River.

foods.name: Local honey
foods.text: A real Lika product, sold at small stalls and shops near the park entrances.
foods.whereToTry: Roadside stalls and shops around the park.

foods.name: Croatian wine
foods.text: Less of a local specialty here than on the coast, though a reasonable selection is available at most restaurants.

foods.name: Fritule (small fried doughnuts)
foods.text: A nice sweet treat after a long day of walking, found at cafés near the park.

accommodation.intro: Accommodation clusters right around the park's entrances, with a few more characterful options in nearby villages.

areas.name: Near Entrance 1 or 2
areas.bestFor: Being as close as possible to the park itself
areas.text: Hotels and guesthouses within walking distance of the main entrances.

areas.name: Nearby villages

gettingThere.intro: Plitvice Lakes is reached by road, sitting roughly halfway between Zagreb and the Dalmatian coast.

options.text: The easiest option without a car, taking about two to 2.5 hours.
options.detail: Frequent daily services run from Zagreb's main bus station.

options.mode: Bus or car from Split or Zadar
options.text: Straightforward from the coast, taking around 2.5 to 3.5 hours.
options.detail: A popular stop for those heading between the coast and Zagreb.

options.text: Convenient from either Zagreb or Zadar.
options.detail: Widely available, though an overnight stay allows a much less rushed visit.

options.text: The only way to see the lakes themselves.
options.detail: Marked routes range from about two to eight hours depending on how much you want to cover.

options.text: Useful for covering longer distances between entrances and trailheads.
options.detail: Included in the park entry ticket, running frequently throughout the day.

options.text: The way to connect the Lower and Upper Lakes sections.
options.detail: Also included in the park entry ticket.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for full waterfalls and manageable crowds
bestTime.summary: Plitvice looks different across the seasons, with each bringing its own case for a visit.

seasons.text: Lush and green, with waterfalls at their fullest after spring rain and snowmelt.
The busiest season, with the boardwalks sometimes crowded at peak midday hours.
Spectacular forest colour reflected in the still-turquoise water, with thinner crowds than summer.
Magical under snow and ice, though some trails close and opening hours shorten.

bestTime.avoid: Peak midday hours in July and August, when the most popular boardwalk sections get crowded.

itinerary.title: One day at Plitvice Lakes
itinerary.intro: A single full day covering both the Lower and Upper Lakes.

days.title: Lower and Upper Lakes
days.summary: A full day of boardwalks, waterfalls and a boat crossing.
days.morning: The Lower Lakes and Veliki Slap.
days.afternoon: Cross Lake Kozjak by boat and explore the Upper Lakes.
days.evening: Dinner near the park before departing or settling in for the night.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Plitvice Lakes visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book park entry tickets online ahead — daily visitor numbers are capped in peak season.
Wear non-slip shoes — boardwalks get damp and slippery, especially near waterfalls.
Start early to see the most popular sections before the day's crowds build.
Bring water and snacks — options inside the park itself are limited.
Pack a light rain layer, even in summer — weather can shift quickly in the hills.
Never swim in the lakes — it's prohibited throughout the park to protect the ecosystem.

faq.q: How many days do you need at Plitvice Lakes?
faq.a: One full day covers both the Lower and Upper Lakes comfortably; an overnight stay allows a more relaxed pace.

faq.q: Can you swim in Plitvice Lakes?
faq.a: No, not — swimming is prohibited throughout the national park to protect the travertine formations and ecosystem.

faq.q: Is Plitvice Lakes worth visiting from Zagreb or the coast?
faq.a: Yes — it's Croatia's most celebrated natural attraction, and its position makes it an easy stop between the two.
A fair amount — even a focused route covers several kilometres of boardwalks and trails.

faq.q: Do you need to book tickets ahead?
faq.a: Yes, recommended in peak season — daily visitor numbers are capped and popular dates can sell out.

faq.q: Is Plitvice Lakes worth visiting in winter?
faq.a: Yes — the frozen waterfalls and snow-covered boardwalks offer a completely different, quieter experience.
